title: Years between total eclipses at the same spot, by luck

source.name: Eclipse path recurrence data
source.publisher: Great American Eclipse / NASA Eclipse Website

notes: Carbondale/Makanda, Illinois sat in the path of totality for BOTH the Aug 21, 2017 and Apr 8, 2024 total solar eclipses -- just 7 years apart, which Southern Illinois University event staff called 'literally unheard of.' The global average wait for any one spot is about 375 years (Jean Meeus 1982 / NASA eclipse catalog); some unlucky locations wait over 1,000 years between totalities.
